status: CORRECTED: owner reports the same brick successfully powers the AP through an ISR4321 NIM-ES2-8-P. Withdraw the brick-fault working diagnosis. Standalone zero readings are preserved as limited-condition observations; C8235 compatibility and PoE hardware/detection remain unresolved.
request: Owner asks how to perform a loaded test or known-good comparison after A-D zero volts and supply-label identification.
target: Detached Flextronics FA230LM1-00 / 341-0703-01 external brick, not router PCB. Pin correspondence from supply-label.json.
known_equipment: Fluke 111, Jesverty source supply, owner-confirmed 1/2 W resistor assortment and assembled 149.8-ohm breadboard. Owner reports two stripped wires and no mating connector. Historical probe tips/hooks are not established as suitable for this connector.
question_pending: Await owner completion of the single-supply transfer back to assembled C8235-A, its boot/USB state and exclusive console ownership before fresh read-only diagnosis.
qualification_before_connection: Verify actual resistor values, 1/2 W ratings, network resistance and secure separated mounting. Current design calculations keep each part below about 0.17 W at the stated voltages; ordinary single resistors are not substituted for the earlier 10 W loads.

Establish a secure insulated test connection, with no stray strands able to bridge contacts and leads restrained against withdrawal. A correctly mating connector/breakout is preferred. Do not assume a computer PSU cable has the same pinout. Owner reports correcting the photographed connection; do not imply this was independently re-photographed or pull-tested.
Reconfirm brick AC disconnected and DC plug detached from router, check for residual voltage before resistance/continuity checks, and record meter lead baseline for connection mapping.
Keep the 12 V return and PoE return separate. No connection to the Jesverty output, PC/programmer or router. Fluke remains COM/V in DC-voltage mode, not an across-output current measurement.
limits: These adapted loads are lighter than the original proposal: 12 V bank about 82 mA/1.01 W at 12.3 V; later PoE bank about 17.1 mA/0.91 W at 53.5 V. Calculated individual dissipation is about 0.168 W and 0.152 W respectively. They are preliminary light-load checks, not manufacturer minimum-load or full-power acceptance tests. Stable outputs would demonstrate operation at those loads only; zero output still does not exclude an undocumented higher minimum-load requirement. Do not connect the 150-ohm bank to 53.5 V, and do not tie the output returns together. No source-supply backfeed, energized rewiring, improvised short or new router-board access.
alternative: Supply replacement as defective is not supported by the current ISR4321 success. Compatibility comparison remains a possible later step after reviewing C8235 PoE hardware/detection.

references.use: Power-resistor heating and ambient-temperature derating; actual selected parts still unconfirmed.
Use COM/V for voltage; current-input measurements across an output would short the circuit.

owner_inventory.source: Current owner report; earlier project notes independently recorded 100 ohm, 1/2 W parts.

original_planned_stages: Record a fresh unloaded B-E voltage and A-D voltage after AC is applied, then disconnect AC.
With AC disconnected and residual voltage checked, attach only the qualified 47 ohm load across B-E. Apply AC and record B-E and A-D voltages. Disconnect AC before changes.

After removing AC and checking residual voltage, add the separate qualified 1 kohm load across D-A. Apply AC and record both voltages for a brief initial observation (about 15-30 seconds), then disconnect AC and let resistors cool.
original_proposal_status: Separate 10 W parts are not available according to owner; retain the prior plan as history only. Current lower-power resistor banks below supersede it as the immediate proposal.

Owner reports 0 VDC X-Y with this 3093-ohm bank on D/A while the separate 12 V bank remains at 12.15 V.

Reconfirm live identity and exclusive console before any connection; then inspect C8235 power/PoE status read-only.
Retain standalone readings and the superseded diagnosis as history, with the ISR4321 success as the current correction. No further resistor loads or speculative pin/return links.

bank_measurements.source: Owner report: built the described breadboard; 149.8 ohms input to output.
bank_measurements.bank: 12 V, six 100 ohm 1/2 W parts, two parallel branches of three in series as requested.
bank_measurements.instrument: Fluke 111 established earlier; reply to unpowered resistance-check request.
bank_measurements.interpretation: Equivalent-resistance sanity check matches 150 ohms within about 0.13%. This is not independent verification of every component or breadboard connection.
bank_measurements.state_limit: No assembly photo or lead baseline supplied; current AC/DC isolation and mating connection question pending.

endpoint_clarification.owner_confirmation: Owner confirms the earlier 149.8-ohm result was the same requested measurement across the two free blue wire ends, including bank and wiring. No repeat measurement was needed.
endpoint_clarification.supersedes: Earlier distinction between a bank-only measurement and a pending full-wire measurement is resolved by this clarification.

bank_measurements.source: Owner reports: that board is built ... X to Y resistance is 3093 ohms.
bank_measurements.bank: PoE candidate, six 4.7 kohm 1/2 W resistors, three parallel branches of two series parts as instructed.
bank_measurements.instrument: Fluke 111 established; owner responds to the isolated unpowered resistance-check request.
bank_measurements.interpretation: Approximately 1.29% below the nominal 3133.33-ohm network, consistent with an approximate 3.13-kohm bank. The total-resistance observation is not independent verification of every component or connection.

connection_report.source: Owner says: I stripped two wires that stick in pretty good; I do not have any type of mating connector.
connection_report.observed_photo: Existing IMG_1319 shows the six recessed socket contacts without these new wires. No photograph of the proposed wiring has been supplied.
connection_report.assessment: Friction fit alone does not establish a retained, insulated test connection. Loose wires could withdraw, expose metal or bridge neighboring contacts; do not energize this unverified arrangement.
connection_report.next_evidence: With AC unplugged and DC disconnected from router, obtain a close-up of the actual connector/wires and breadboard before selecting a suitable connection method.

photo_review.method: Viewed both original photos at default and original resolution; no image alteration.
observations: IMG_1322 shows six blue axial resistors and jumper wiring on a breadboard. Several jumper endpoints are obscured; the photo alone does not prove every connection.

IMG_1323 shows a latch-right plug. Two turquoise insulated wires occupy the lower-left and middle-right cavities. Stranded copper is visible, especially splayed outside the lower-left cavity. No short between contacts is visible.
The plug is detached from the router in the photos. AC connection and the entire path from blue wires to breadboard are outside the photographed area.
photo_review.pin_inference: Rotating the established latch-up A/B/C over D/E/F map clockwise gives D/A, E/B, F/C rows in the latch-right view. Thus lower-left is F/P3 and middle-right is B/P5. The photographed B/F pair is valid for the 12 V load; F, like E, is labeled GROUND. This is not the A/D PoE pair.
photo_review.initial_assessment: Correct 12 V contact grouping, but exposed/splayed copper and no independently established retention prompted an unpowered correction before energization.
photo_review.superseding_owner_report: Owner subsequently states: it is fixed, it is not near anything but plastic. Treat as an owner-reported correction, not a new photograph or independent retention test.
photo_review.scope: No router access, electrical measurement by the agent, powered load test or confirmed PoE repair.

powered_observations.source: Owner reports 12.15 vdc and then constant in response to the first powered-check instructions.
powered_observations.target: Detached Flextronics FA230LM1-00 / 341-0703-01 external brick; router not part of requested circuit.
powered_observations.meter: Fluke 111; requested DC volts, COM/V-ohm, across the two bank input points.
powered_observations.interpretation: 12 V output supplies this approximately 81.1 mA / 0.985 W load at a constant reported voltage. This does not establish full output capacity, PoE output operation or router compatibility.
powered_observations.state_limit: Owner response to instructions keeping router detached and unplugging AC afterward; elapsed time, meter display and final AC removal were not independently captured.

powered_observations.source: Owner reports: with 12.15 vdc across load ... I get -.002 vdc from D to A.
powered_observations.target: Same detached Flextronics FA230LM1-00 / 341-0703-01 external brick in the requested router-disconnected test.
powered_observations.stage: 12 V load retained; separate PoE output voltage measured without a PoE load
powered_observations.requested_meter_setup: Fluke 111 DC volts, black D/red A; requested reading after 10-15 seconds, followed by AC unplug.
powered_observations.interpretation: Effectively zero relative to the nominal -53.5 V output. The approximately 81.1 mA load on the 12 V rail did not bring up the PoE output. This narrows the observation to the external brick/output cable/contact path under these conditions; it is not a router configuration measurement.
powered_observations.limits: Owner report, without meter photo or separately confirmed duration/settling/final AC removal. PoE-specific loading has not been tested; no verified minimum-load specification or full-load result is available. Do not classify the supply as conclusively failed or infer a router-only repair from this result.

powered_observations.source: Owner reports: I am still getting 0 vdc x to y ... but 12.15 vdc f to b.
powered_observations.target: Same Flextronics FA230LM1-00 / 341-0703-01 external brick; response to the requested router-disconnected dual-load test.
powered_observations.meter: Fluke 111; requested DC volts with COM/V-ohm leads, measurement at bank connection points.
powered_observations.stability_reported: Owner says still 0 for X-Y; stability/duration not separately quantified in this reply. Earlier 12.15 V reading was explicitly constant.
powered_observations.interpretation: The added 3093-ohm load did not produce a measurable PoE output while the 12 V load still had 12.15 V. The stated 17.3 mA/0.925 W PoE-bank calculation is prospective at 53.5 V, not current or power delivered during this zero-volt test.
powered_observations.state_limit: Owner report without an independent meter/connection capture; requested separate-bank wiring, router disconnection and final AC unplug were not independently observed.

requested_dual_load_test.preconditions: AC unplugged, router disconnected; Fluke DC-voltage check that both outputs have fallen to approximately zero before wiring. Secure insulated connections; no shared breadboard rail or return between the banks.
requested_dual_load_test.poe_load: Connect separate 3093-ohm bank X to D and Y to A.
requested_dual_load_test.meter: Fluke 111 DC volts, black COM/red V-ohm; no resistance or current-mode measurement across energized outputs.
requested_dual_load_test.sequence: Apply AC; read new bank black X/red Y (nominal -53.5 V if active), then original bank black F/red B at breadboard connection points. Record stability; unplug AC after about 15-30 seconds, before any wiring change.
requested_dual_load_test.status: Owner-reported result received: PoE X-Y 0 VDC; 12 V F-B 12.15 VDC. No further repetition selected.

diagnostic_conclusion.current_evidence: Same brick works for owner-reported ISR4321/NIM-ES2-8-P/AP PoE operation.
diagnostic_conclusion.correction: Previous brick/output-path-fault inference is superseded; the standalone resistor tests were not a sufficient qualification test for this supply.
diagnostic_conclusion.unresolved: Mechanism behind different standalone versus installed behavior, exact C8235/prototype supply compatibility, and C8235 PoE circuitry/presence/detection. Do not infer a dedicated enable/ID pin or a jumper from this result.
diagnostic_conclusion.next: Fresh read-only C8235 diagnosis after owner moves the only PoE supply back and confirms physical/USB/console state. Preserve all prior test readings.

reference_followup.result: No verified exact-model minimum-load or enable specification obtained. Cisco production-router power table lists PWR-CC1-230WAC for C8235-G2, with 12 V/9 A and -54 V/2.45 A. This is a production reference, not confirmation that the current FA230LM1-00 is equivalent or that a replacement is compatible with this prototype.

conclusion.observed: Unloaded A/D about zero; with 149.8-ohm 12 V load, A/D -0.002 V and B/F 12.15 V; with both 149.8-ohm B/F and 3093-ohm D/A loads, PoE-bank X/Y 0 V and 12 V F/B 12.15 V.
conclusion.working_diagnosis: External brick PoE output circuitry or its output cable/contact path is the leading suspect. Do not treat this adapter as a known-good PoE source for further router diagnosis.
conclusion.not_established: Exact failed component, proper behavior at the manufacturer-specified minimum/full load, current brick compatibility with this prototype, and router PoE-controller/hardware health. These light loads do not conclusively exclude undocumented minimum-load or control behavior.
conclusion.decision: Stop repeated or arbitrarily heavier resistor tests. Unplug AC; remove test wiring only after output voltage has fallen near zero. Preserve the sealed supply and the independent resistor banks.
conclusion.next: Compare with a verified-working supply confirmed compatible with this exact router/connector/pinout, or have this brick and its cable checked on a qualified bench using applicable specifications. Revisit router PoE detection only after a working external PoE rail is established.
conclusion.router_scope: No new router access or configuration/firmware/security change; router operational PoE remains unresolved.
